title: Playing for troops at Jefferson Barracks and losing musicians to the services
summary: They play free shows at Jefferson Barracks, then lose Charles, Chester Lane and others to the Navy at Great Lakes in September 1942.

story.theme_name: Drafted: musicians in the military and the war years
story.community_name: Drafted: service bands, USO shows and the war years

blocks.x: In the meantime, we had been taking our band down to the Jefferson Barracks, playing for the troops about twice a month, free of charge. We would take the entire show and band down, and the troops seemed like they enjoyed it so much. And we enjoyed doing it. The latter part of 1942, we began losing

September of '42, that's right. We began losing members of the band to the Army, to the Navy, to the Air Force. A friend of mine, a friend of ours, rather, Bowden, had joined the Navy in Chicago, and he was recruiting men, musicians, for the Navy up at Great Lakes. And the old fox did a wonderful job in recruiting band boys from St. Louis. My brother Charles went, several of the other fellows in the band went.
You lost a guitar player, a trumpet player --

Chester Lane, the piano player. So that just went through the band like Grant went through Richmond. But the people kept coming to the club and we kept playing those special requests. And they would say, 'Pillars,' we know you're doing the best you can. And we still love you and
we'll keep coming." And I was able to fill in with various musicians here and there, to keep the band going. But those were the highlights of 1942.
